uncited: This method generates a voxel mipmap pyramid from a clipmap-based volume representation using GPU compute shaders.

It solves the problem of efficiently downsampling high-resolution voxel data into lower-resolution levels for rendering or lighting calculations, specifically tailored for clipmap architectures where data is organized in circular buffers or layered structures.

It differs from standard texture downsampling by explicitly managing the transition from the clipmap's specific memory layout (involving `LayoutSize` and `ClipMapCount`) to a linear mipmap array, requiring intermediate textures to avoid read-write conflicts.

If any resolution dimension is smaller than the corresponding `threadGroupCounts` dimension, divide `threadGroupCounts` by 4 and clamp to a minimum of 1.

This method is implemented in the Xenko VoxelGI project, an unofficial extension or fork related to the Xenko game engine.
It is designed for voxel-based global illumination (GI) systems that utilize clipmaps for efficient memory management of large voxel worlds.
